vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: baoyu-post-to-weibo
Version: 1.103.1

The skill bundle provides sophisticated automation for posting content to Weibo by controlling a Chrome instance via the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP). It employs high-risk capabilities to bypass anti-bot measures, including simulating real system keystrokes (Cmd+V/Ctrl+V) via AppleScript and PowerShell (paste-from-clipboard.ts), and managing system processes using pkill and ps aux (weibo-utils.ts). The SKILL.md instructions explicitly direct the AI agent to autonomously kill Chrome processes and retry operations upon failure. While these behaviors are technically aligned with the stated purpose of automating a complex web interface, the combination of process management, raw input simulation, and automated retry logic represents a significant attack surface and high-risk behavior profile.

llm.summary: The skill's code, dependencies, and runtime instructions are consistent with its stated purpose (automating Weibo posting via a real Chrome instance); it does read and reuse local Chrome profiles and spawns local tools, which is expected but has privacy implications the user should consider.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (post to Weibo via Chrome) match what the package contains: TypeScript scripts for regular posts and articles, a Chrome CDP helper, Markdown → HTML conversion, and clipboard/paste helpers. Required runtimes (bun or npx) and use of a real Chrome instance are appropriate for the stated functionality.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to run local scripts under scripts/ and to read EXTEND.md preference files in project/home/XDG config paths; the included code also searches for and may reuse existing Chrome user-data directories and DevToolsActivePort files so it can attach to a logged-in browser session. That behavior is coherent with the goal (bypass anti-bots by using a real browser) but means the skill will read local browser state (profiles/devtools files) and interact with the clipboard and system input for paste keystrokes.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No remote install/downloads or hidden installers are present in the registry metadata; this is an instruction+source bundle with no external URL downloads. Requiring bun or npx is proportional. All code is included in the skill bundle (no opaque network install step).
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No environment variables or external credentials are requested. However, the code intentionally accesses local Chrome user-data directories and DevToolsActivePort files to discover or reuse running Chrome sessions — this is necessary to leverage an already-logged-in browser, but it means browser cookies/sessions could be accessed indirectly by the skill's process. No unrelated secrets or cloud credentials are requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always: true and does not assert persistent system-wide changes. It will spawn local processes and read/write temporary files during operation (normal for this functionality) and may reuse or open a Chrome profile; it does not modify other skills or system-wide agent configuration.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be what it says: it automates posting by controlling a real Chrome browser and using clipboard/paste to avoid bot detection. Before installing, consider: 1) Privacy: the skill searches and may reuse your Chrome user-data directories and DevToolsActivePort to attach to logged-in sessions — if you want to avoid exposing other accounts, use a dedicated Chrome profile for Weibo or a temporary profile. 2) Inspect & run locally: the full source is included, so manually review any code you are uncomfortable with (it spawns processes and reads files). 3) Permissions: the scripts will require local executables (bun or npx) and may need clipboard and accessibility permissions (for synthetic keystrokes) on your OS. 4) Isolation: if you are unsure, run the scripts in an isolated environment (VM/container) or create a separate browser profile. 5) No network exfiltration endpoints were found in metadata — nevertheless, only supply credentials by logging into Chrome yourself (the skill does not ask for API keys).
